channel.title: Gentse cultuuragenda
channel.description: Daily screenings at Ghent's arthouse cinemas and film clubs, rarest films first, with who paid for each film. Kinepolis not included.

    Funding: A Flemish youth film produced by Ivy Vanhaecke at deMENSEN, with Germany's CALA Filmproduktion and Juliet at Pupkin. LevelK sells it abroad. The listing we found names no public funds.
  16. Monster Mia (4× this week): Studio Skoop 14:30
    Funding: arx anima (AT) with Arxlight Pictures, Ikiru Films (ES) and Peng! Boom! Tschak! (DE); sales Sola Media. Funds and budget unknown.
  17. Primetime (4× this week): Studio Skoop 17:15
    Funding: A24 both finances and distributes this one. Robert Pattinson produces through his company Icki Eneo Arlo, with Range Media Partners and Square Peg also credited. No budget has been published.
  18. Coyote vs. Acme (4× this week): Sphinx 17:30
    Funding: Warner Bros. paid the $70M production, then shelved it; Ketchup Entertainment paid $50M to release it.
  19. Iron Boy NV (4× this week): Sphinx 17:30
  20. Orphée et Eurydice (4× this week): Opera Ballet Vlaanderen 20:00
  21. Mumbo Jumbo (6× this week): Studio Skoop 11:00; Sphinx 14:30
    Funding: A.Film A/S (DK); sales by LevelK. Funds and budget unknown.
  22. The Devils (6× this week): Studio Skoop 22:15
    Funding: Russo Productions; Warner Bros. distributed. Budget unknown.
  23. The Texas Chain Saw Massacre (6× this week): Studio Skoop 22:15
    Funding: Vortex Inc.; Bill Parsley's MAB Inc. put in $60,000 for 50% of the film. Budget $80,000–140,000 (sources give up to $300,000).
  24. Moulin (7× this week): Sphinx 14:15
  25. The Only Living Pickpocket in New York (7× this week): Studio Skoop 19:45
    Funding: Produced by T-Street, financed by MRC. Budget unknown.
  26. Hope (8× this week): Sphinx 17:00; Studio Skoop 21:45
    Funding: Plus M Entertainment invests and distributes. Budget about ₩70 billion (≈ $46M), reported as Korea's most expensive film.
  27. Digger (13× this week): Sphinx 11:00 · 20:30; Studio Skoop 22:00
    Funding: A Hollywood studio picture: Legendary Pictures produced it in partnership with Warner Bros., which also distributes it. Tom Cruise is a producer alongside Iñárritu and Mary Parent. Warner Bros. says the budget stayed at $125 million; reports of $160–180 million were denied by the studio.
  28. Sense and Sensibility (13× this week): Studio Skoop 14:30; Sphinx 20:15
    Funding: Working Title Films produced it with November Pictures and Kiddo Films. Working Title belongs to Universal, which releases the film internationally while its arthouse label Focus Features handles the US.
  29. Shaun het Schaap: Het Beest op de Boerderij (14× this week): Studio Skoop 11:00 · 14:30; Sphinx 14:30
    Funding: Aardman made it as a Sky Original: Sky releases it in the UK and StudioCanal everywhere else. Original title The Beast of Mossy Bottom.
  30. Wicker (14× this week): Studio Skoop 17:15
    Funding: Financed by Tango and Topic Studios, with development money from Votiv; South of The River and Yoki also produce. Black Bear bought it at Sundance 2026 for North America and the UK and handles international sales.
  31. The Invite (15× this week): Sphinx 17:30; Studio Skoop 19:45
    Funding: Produced by Megan Ellison's Annapurna, then sold at Sundance 2026. A24 won a days-long bidding war against Focus Features and paid more than $12 million for the rights.
  32. La Gradiva (25× this week): Sphinx 11:00 · 20:15; Studio Skoop 17:00 · 19:30
    Funding: Les Films du Poisson (FR) with Bibi Film TV (IT). CNC €70,000 and Italy's MIC €70,000 in French-Italian co-production aid; budget unknown.
  33. Wild Horse Nine (37× this week): Studio Skoop 11:00 · 14:30 · 17:00 · 19:45; Sphinx 14:30 · 20:30
    Funding: Blueprint Pictures and Film4; Searchlight Pictures distributes. Budget unknown.
  34. Coward (43× this week): Studio Skoop 11:00 · 14:30 · 17:00 · 19:45 · 22:15; Sphinx 17:30 · 20:30
    Funding: Lukas Dhont's third feature is led by his Belgian company The Reunion, with Lumen (France), Topkapi Films (Netherlands) and Versus (Belgium) as co-producers. Brussels' regional fund put in €125,000, which it lists as about 1.2% of the budget, so the film cost roughly €10 million. The Match Factory sells it abroad and Diaphana releases it in France.
